CVE-2026-120474.title: undici vulnerable to cross-user cache disclosure via same-origin redirect
CVE-2026-120474.description: undici is an HTTP client for Node.js. In versions 7.0.0 through 7.30.1 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.3, when the redirect interceptor and a shared response cache are used together, an authenticated request that is redirected to a same-origin target has the final response stored under the original request's cache key. That key omits the credential and carries no Vary header, so a later anonymous or different user can be served the first user's private response body. This results in cross-user disclosure of cached private responses. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.2 and 8.12.4, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later.

CVE-2026-135403.title: Ever Gauzy: Login rate-limiting is bypassable via spoofed CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers, enabling unlimited password guessing
CVE-2026-135403.description: Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.44.2, getTracker in packages/core/src/lib/throttler/throttler-behind-proxy.guard.ts accepts CF-Connecting-IP without verifying that a trusted Cloudflare edge supplied it; when CF-Connecting-IP is absent, app.set('trust proxy', true) can let an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For value determine req.ip. In deployments where a trusted intermediary does not overwrite these headers, or where the firewall permits direct API access, varying the applicable header on repeated POST /auth/login requests gives an unauthenticated remote attacker a distinct throttle bucket for each attempt, so the five-attempts-per-60-seconds limit does not trigger and no account lockout, CAPTCHA, or exponential backoff limits password guessing. This issue is fixed in version 111.44.2.

CVE-2026-74759.title: Google::Auth versions 0.12 for Perl allow server side request forgery via unvalidated credential_source URLs in AWS external account credentials
CVE-2026-74759.description:
Google::Auth versions 0.12 for Perl allow server side request forgery via unvalidated credential_source URLs in AWS external account credentials.

An external_account configuration with the AWS subject token type selects Google::Auth::ExternalAccountCredentials::Aws. Its retrieve_subject_token sends requests to the imdsv2_session_token_url, url and region_url fields of credential_source without the host check that the other credential classes apply.

Any caller that builds credentials from a configuration it does not fully control issues GET and PUT requests to hosts the configuration names, including internal services and link-local metadata endpoints.

CVE-2026-99530.title: cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes
CVE-2026-99530.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes

With favordynmods enabled, a cgroup.procs migration takes the target
threadgroup's cgroup_threadgroup_rwsem for writing. A process fork holds
the forking threadgroup's semaphore for reading. These are different
semaphores when fork creates a new process.

copy_process() publishes the child's PID before cgroup_post_fork() links
the child to its css_set. A writer can find the child in that interval,
take its uncontended semaphore, and migrate it while child->cgroups still
points to init_css_set and child->cg_list is empty. Migration links the
node into init_css_set.mg_tasks. cgroup_post_fork() then adds the same
node to the intended css_set as though it were unlinked, corrupting both
task lists and their css_set ownership.

This regresses the fork/migration race fixed by commit b12b533fa523
("cgroups: add lock for child->cgroups in cgroup_post_fork()")…

CVE-2026-99628.title: drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins
CVE-2026-99628.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Avoid closing unowned DDC pins

[WHY]
dal_ddc_open() cleans up pins it acquires on later failures. If the
data-pin open fails, this attempt acquired nothing. If opening the
clock pin or configuring fails, dal_ddc_open() closes the pins it
opened. An extra dal_ddc_close() is unnecessary and unsafe:
GPIO_RESULT_ALREADY_OPENED can mean AUX owns the existing handles,
and closing them here would disrupt AUX.

[HOW]
Remove the extra dal_ddc_close() from the failed-open path.

(cherry picked from commit 175ae7772b68757b4932f34ff862923cab7abe21)

CVE-2026-99761.title: batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT
CVE-2026-99761.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT

batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free()
before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can
therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times
out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which
loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:

CPU0 CPU1
batadv_tt_free() batadv_purge_orig()
batadv_tt_global_del_orig()
hash = ...tt.global_hash;
batadv_tt_global_table_free()
batadv_hash_destroy(hash);
spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);

Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after
the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second
disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because
it is free'd anyway.
